title: Chapter 10 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of packaging, cooking, deployment, and optimisation!

questions.question: Which build configuration is intended for final player distribution?
questions.explanation: Shipping builds are optimised and stripped of editor/debug content.

questions.question: What does 'cooking' assets mean?
options: Converting editor assets to platform‑specific formats
questions.explanation: Cooking transforms raw .uassets into optimised data for the target platform.

questions.question: Packaged games include the Unreal Editor.
questions.explanation: Packaged builds contain only the runtime necessary to play the game, not the editor tools.

questions.question: Which menu path starts the packaging process?
questions.explanation: File → Package Project lets you choose a platform to build.

questions.question: The _____ Default Map in Project Settings defines which level loads when the packaged game starts.
questions.explanation: Game Default Map is the first level loaded in standalone builds.

questions.question: What does 'Create Compressed Cooked Packages' do?
options: Reduces package size but may increase load times
questions.explanation: It compresses cooked data to save disk space at the cost of CPU decompression on load.

questions.question: What must you have to build an iOS package?
options: A Mac with Xcode and Apple Developer account
questions.explanation: iOS compilation requires macOS and Xcode.

questions.question: What is the default graphics API for modern Android builds?
questions.explanation: Vulkan is the recommended modern API for Android in Unreal Engine.

questions.question: You can build a console (Xbox/PlayStation) package without being a registered developer.
questions.explanation: Console development requires NDAs, dev kits, and SDK access.

questions.question: Which view mode shows material expense as a heatmap?
questions.explanation: Shader Complexity (Alt+8) uses green (cheap) to red (expensive) to indicate material cost.

questions.question: What command shows real‑time frame rate in the console?
questions.explanation: `stat fps` displays frames per second; `stat unit` shows detailed frame timings.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `ProfileGPU` command?
options: To capture a single frame's rendering timeline
questions.explanation: ProfileGPU provides a detailed breakdown of GPU time per pass.

questions.question: Which of the following reduces CPU overhead?
options: Using Event Tick on all actors
questions.explanation: Timers run at intervals, reducing per‑frame CPU work compared to Tick.

questions.question: What is actor pooling?
options: Reusing existing actors instead of spawn/destroy
questions.explanation: Pooling reduces the cost of spawn/destroy by recycling objects.

questions.question: What does 'stat streaming' monitor?
questions.explanation: Stat streaming shows real‑time texture and mesh streaming usage.

questions.question: Why should you disable Tick on actors that don't need it?
options: It wastes CPU time every frame
questions.explanation: Tick runs every frame; disabling it on idle actors saves CPU.

questions.question: Packaged builds always include the Unreal Editor console.
questions.explanation: Shipping builds do not include the console or editor features.

questions.question: What is the benefit of iterative cooking?
options: It only cooks assets that changed since last cook
questions.explanation: Iterative cooking saves time by only processing modified assets.

questions.question: Which setting makes a packaged build as small as possible?
questions.explanation: Compression reduces file size. For Distribution also strips debug info.

questions.question: What tool should you use for comprehensive CPU/GPU profiling over time?
questions.explanation: Unreal Insights records a complete trace of performance data for in‑depth analysis.
